title: fix: derive monitor model category from catalog metadata
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
The `community/` prefix rename (#14621) turned every legacy community ID into an alias, so all pre-rename traffic now arrives in the model monitor as a historical alias row. Those rows took their category from the recorded event type instead of the catalog.

- Endpoints are coarser than categories: video and 3D both record `generate.image`, so `NamanSoni78/Seedance-2.5` showed under Image instead of Video
- `mergeModelHealth` now reads `type`, `endpointType` and `community` from the aliased catalog entry
- Event type stays the fallback for genuinely unregistered traffic (deleted community endpoints)
- Recorded health is still kept separate from the canonical model, unchanged

Verified against the live catalog and `/v1/models/status`: 225 alias-resolvable rows, one category mismatch before the fix, none after. Scope (Official/Community) was already correct via `provider`.

gist.headline: The catalog knows best
gist.blurb: The model monitor stopped guessing what kind of flower it was looking at. Historical community aliases now consult the catalog, so Seedance-2.5 can bloom under Video instead of wandering into Image.
gist.summary: Fixed model-monitor category resolution for legacy `community/` aliases by reading `type`, `endpointType`, and `community` from the aliased catalog entry, while retaining recorded event type as a fallback for unregistered endpoints.
gist.impact: `/v1/models/status` now categorizes alias-resolvable models from catalog metadata—correcting the Seedance-2.5 Video-versus-Image mismatch and bringing the verified mismatch count from one to zero across 225 alias rows.

Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses and carrying a catalog card, notices the correct metadata; a friendly CRT monitor robot confirms the classification while code-vines and flowers make the catalog feel alive.
